<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

Subject: Re: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

Thank you for your email. I've reviewed my lease, and I believe the $75 late fee on this month's rent may not be applicable.

Section 4.2 of the lease states that rent is due on the 1st, with a grace period through the 5th, and that no late fees may be charged during the grace period. My rent payment was received on the 3rd, which falls within that grace period, so I don't believe a late fee should have been assessed.

I'd appreciate it if you could review the account and remove the $75 charge. Please let me know if you need any documentation from my end, such as proof of when the payment was sent.

Thank you for your help with this. I look forward to your confirmation.

Best regards,
[Your name]
Unit 3B

---

A few tips before sending:

- **Attach proof of payment** if you have it (bank statement, portal confirmation, or check image with a date).
- **Keep a copy** of this email and any reply for your records.
- If they refuse to remove the fee, you can escalate by sending a formal written notice referencing Section 4.2 (Section 9.4 confirms email is an acceptable form of written notice). Depending on your state or city, tenant rights organizations or local housing offices can also help.
